newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares sag through day, end off almost 1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares sag through day, end off almost 1 pct.

text.p: The Dutch share market slipped steadily from opening gains on Wednesday and received a late shove down from U.S. figures, traders said.
The AEX index of the 25 leading stocks ended 6.79 points, or 0.92 percent, lower at 729.58 points.

The index began promisingly, opening up almost 3 points, but had shed almost almost all its gains by midsession, before stronger than forecast March industrial production data re-enforced the weaker trend.
The losses followed a 20 point rise on Tuesday.
Traders said the market slipped as some players took profit and as a number of options traders happily sold the market down to benefit their positions ahead of the expiry of April options on Friday.
"The market makers with (April AEX) 740 calls did some short-covering yesterday, fearing a rise would trigger a short squeeze. They're selling today," one trader said.
Traders added the weaker dollar helped push prices down.

Photocopier maker Oce van der Grinten was the largest loser among the leading companies. Its shares lost 11.50 guilders, ending at 227.80. The shares were trading ex-dividend, but the bulk of the losses were a reaction to Oce's first quarter results published late on Tuesday.

Its sales rose by 55 percent to 1.20 billion guilders, but largely through acquisitions and currency effects. Excluding acquisitions, sales rose 10 percent of which eight percent was generated through favourable exchange rates.
"The figures were not so very good. The organic growth was only two percent which is rather disappointing," one trader said.
